source_state: uncommitted retained native residency inventory, synchronous array readiness and cross-unit owner preflight
behavior: RetainedStorage deduplicates completed native allocation capacities, immutable host-transfer owners and exact checkpoint source payloads while retaining the physical owners.
Narrow array views preserve full backing capacity; shared inventories and host/source aliases do not multiply physical bytes.
Original handles and manager entries may be dropped or evicted while the inventory keeps their payloads valid; releasing the inventory releases its ownership.
Lazy, custom, unknown-source, in-flight and failed-transfer resources cannot produce a complete bound. An unknown snapshot remains unknown after external completion.
Residency inspection bypasses recovery reaping and performs no native completion polling, materialization, source reads or eviction.
The synchronous transfer boundary finalizes output array readiness before publishing the exact transfer generation, while retaining normal recovery and failure handling.

The neutral controller validates global aliases; native preflight checks only physical owner recipes against exact per-unit sources. The enabled cross-unit regression verifies one shared host capacity through eviction and reacquisition.
Capacity conflicts and arithmetic overflow reject rather than undercount.
limits: This inventory covers the supplied owners and current residency-manager storage, not all model memory or future allocations.

Loaded module replacements, addressable parameter banks, decoder state, returned output handles and other retained owners still require composition; materialization and streaming need separate future workspace bounds.
Custom-backed arrays, including any native host-buffer donation represented by a custom deleter, remain unknown until their ownership can be proved.
Inventory retention is not a ledger pin, a working-memory reservation or permission to allocate. Public native shared-domain pool registration and complete request quotes remain incomplete.
Metadata, allocator cache, JIT, operating-system cache and process memory are outside this physical payload inventory.
No new released-checkpoint numerical comparison or allocator/process peak measurement was made.
Native builds retain the existing compact-unwind linker warning and the feature check reports four existing quote/projection helpers awaiting production integration.
